summary: Thomas R. Trautmann is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and held posts at the University of Michigan, where he was co-director in 1980 and affiliated in 1991.
Thomas Robert Malthus studied at Warrington Academy around 1782–1783, Jesus College, Cambridge in 1784, and the University of Cambridge around 1784–1788.

Thomas Roebuck was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at the Royal High School, Edinburgh. He served as assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George in 1811 and was a member of The Asiatic Society (c. 1811–1819).
Thomas Watters was a scholar in sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his B.A. studies at Queen's University Belfast (1857–1861) and Queen's University of Ireland (c. 1857–1861).
Thomas Zehnder is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Zurich and studied under supervisor Alexander Lubotsky.

Thubten Chodron is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UCLA, USC, Kopan Monastery, and Dorje Pamo Monastery under teachers including Tenzin Gyatso and Thubten Zopa Rinpoche. She directed programs at several centers and founded Sravasti Abbey, serving as abbess.

Thubten Jigme Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley and Ngawang Nyima. He served as director of the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and was a professor at Indiana University (1965–1992).

Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley studied under Trijang Rinpoche and the 13th Dalai Lama. He taught several students, including Dagpo Rinpoche, Tenzin Gyatso, Thubten Jigme Norbu, and Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

Thubten Zopa Rinpoche worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology, studying at Dungkar Monastery and under teachers like Yeshe Thubten and Geshe Rabten. He founded Kopan Monastery, Maitripa College, and FPMT, where he served as spiritual director from 1984.

Thupten Jinpa works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at Zongkar Choede, Ganden Monastery, and Cambridge, he was a fellow at Girton College (1996–1999), visited Stanford (c. 2011–2012), and founded the Institute of Tibetan Classics, serving as chief editor.

Thupten Samphel was a Tibetology scholar who studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi (c. 1974–1979), and Columbia University (c. 1979–1980). He held a post at the Tibet Policy Institute from 2012 to 2018.
Thushini S. Jayawardena is a religious studies scholar who completed a PhD at Auckland University of Technology by 2017 and studied under traditional teacher Satya Narayan Goenka.

Théodore Pavie was an Indology and sinology scholar who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He succeeded Burnouf as Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and taught Hebrew lessons and lectures at the Catholic University of the West in 1862.

Tianshu Zhu works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology, earning an MA at Northwest University and a PhD at Ohio State under John C. Huntington. Zhu held posts at Northwest University, Shaanxi History Museum, Korea University, and Ohio State.

Tilak Kariyawasam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as head of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1993) and Dean of the Graduate School at the International Buddhist College (attested 2014).

Tilmann Vetter was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner and Erich Heintel. He succeeded David Seyfort Ruegg and served as professor at Leiden University from 1974 to 2002.

Timothy Hugh Barrett is a scholar in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied at Cambridge and Yale. He taught at the University of Cambridge (attested 1981) and became a professor at SOAS University of London in 1986.

Timothy Lenz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox. He held posts at the University of Washington, where he was attested as professor in 2017.

Timothy Lubin is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1994. He has been affiliated with Washington and Lee University (attested 2012–2020) and serves as a collaborator on the Dharma Project.
Tina Rasmussen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw and was supervised for her MA by Christian K. Wedemeyer.
